chunks: The chiefs of the people who did not believe and denied the life to come, though We had given them good things of this life to enjoy, (said): 'He is only a mortal like you. He eats as you do, and drinks as you drink.'

key_terms.الْمَلَأُ: The chiefs or elite of the people

ai.seo_question: Why did the disbelievers question the prophet's humanity despite his divine message?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse critiques the 'al-mala' (elite) who reduced prophethood to mere biological functions, arguing that the Prophet's humanity was a prerequisite for relatable guidance rather than a disqualification. Their denial of the Hereafter and attachment to worldly luxury ('atrufnahum') blinded them to the spiritual reality of the messenger, a theme central to the narrative of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) in Surah Al-Mu'minun.
